symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Number of equal clique blocks.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Number of units in each clique block.

symbols.name: V_n
symbols.def: Fixed population \(V_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Generic clique-block index.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Generic label within a clique block.

symbols.name: B_r
symbols.def: Block \(r\) in a fixed labeled partition of \(V_n\), with \(|B_r|=s\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_{b,s}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_{b,s}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_b\}\) is a partition of \(V_n\) into equal blocks.

symbols.name: G_{b,s}
symbols.def: Disjoint union of the complete graphs induced by the blocks in \(\mathcal B_{b,s}\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Generic known simple interference graph on \(V_n\).

symbols.name: H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G)
symbols.def: Two-layer exposure conflict graph for the DTE on \(G\).

symbols.name: \Theta_2(G)
symbols.def: Two-layer target-outcome vectors on \(G\) satisfying a normalized Euclidean-ball constraint in each layer.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Generic experimental-unit index.

symbols.name: \widetilde N_i
symbols.def: Closed neighborhood of unit \(i\) in \(G_{b,s}\); it is the unique block containing \(i\).

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: Generic binary treatment assignment.

symbols.name: z^{\prime}
symbols.def: Second generic treatment assignment.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Fixed schedule \(Y=(Y_i(z):i\in V_n,z\in\mathcal Z_n)\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: DTE exposure-layer index.

symbols.name: e_{i,k}
symbols.def: \(e_{i,0}\) is all control on \(\widetilde N_i\), while \(e_{i,1}\) treats only \(i\).

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: Vector of all \(u_{i,k}\).

symbols.name: \tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)
symbols.def: \(\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}(u_{i,1}-u_{i,0})\).

symbols.name: \Theta_{b,s}
symbols.def: Product of the two normalized Euclidean balls for the control and treated target-outcome layers.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_2(G_{b,s})
symbols.def: Published \(q=2\) arbitrary-neighborhood-interference class specialized to \(G_{b,s}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_n
symbols.def: All randomization laws on binary assignments.

symbols.name: \Gamma_n
symbols.def: All measurable assignment-and-outcome estimators.

symbols.name: R_2(G_{b,s})
symbols.def: Worst-case mean squared error minimized jointly over \(\mathcal D_n\) and \(\Gamma_n\).

symbols.name: H_{b,s}
symbols.def: DTE exposure-level conflict graph induced by \(G_{b,s}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Number of blocks assigned the all-control exposure pattern.

symbols.name: \mathcal S_c
symbols.def: Orbit of maximal compatible exposure sets with exactly \(c\) all-control blocks and one isolated-treated label in each remaining block.

symbols.name: S_c
symbols.def: Fixed canonical representative of orbit \(\mathcal S_c\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Set of all-control blocks, with \(|C|=c\).

symbols.name: J_r
symbols.def: Treated label selected in block \(r\notin C\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Law \(p=(p_0,\ldots,p_b)\) of the all-control block count.

symbols.name: A_c
symbols.def: Common coefficient on each observed isolated-treated outcome when the orbit index is \(c\).

symbols.name: D_c
symbols.def: Common coefficient on each observed control outcome when the orbit index is \(c\).

symbols.name: \delta_{p,A,D}
symbols.def: Block- and unit-invariant randomization and estimator indexed by \(p\), \(A_c\), and \(D_c\).

symbols.name: W_c
symbols.def: Convexified moment matrix with rank-one realization \(W_c=p_c(1,A_c,D_c)^{\mathsf T}(1,A_c,D_c)\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: First coordinate index in a coefficient moment matrix.

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: Second coordinate index in a coefficient moment matrix.

symbols.name: w^c_{\alpha\beta}
symbols.def: Entry \((\alpha,\beta)\) of \(W_c\), ordered as \((1,A_c,D_c)\).

symbols.name: K_0(W)
symbols.def: Two-layer risk matrix on the constant block-mean mode.

symbols.name: K_{\mathrm B}(W)
symbols.def: Two-layer risk matrix on every between-block zero-sum mode.

symbols.name: k_{\mathrm W}(W)
symbols.def: Risk eigenvalue on the treated within-block contrast modes.

symbols.name: \lambda_0
symbols.def: Dual norm multiplier for the control-layer Euclidean ball.

symbols.name: \lambda_1
symbols.def: Dual norm multiplier for the treated-layer Euclidean ball.

symbols.name: V_{b,s}
symbols.def: Optimal value of the explicit mode semidefinite program.

symbols.name: \mathfrak G_{b,s}
symbols.def: Wreath-product permutations of blocks and labels within blocks, augmented by simultaneous sign reversal of both outcome layers.

symbols.name: g_{\mathrm B}
symbols.def: For \(b\ge2\), \(g_{\mathrm B}=(2s)^{-1/2}(\mathbf 1_{B_1}-\mathbf 1_{B_2})\); for \(b=1\), set \(g_{\mathrm B}=0\).

symbols.name: g_{\mathrm W}
symbols.def: \(g_{\mathrm W}=2^{-1/2}(\mathbf e_{(1,1)}-\mathbf e_{(1,2)})\), using the first two labels of block \(B_1\).

symbols.name: P_c
symbols.def: Orthogonal coordinate projection onto the target outcomes revealed by the canonical maximal exposure pattern \(S_c\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{b,s}^{\star}
symbols.def: Finite atom dictionary produced from an optimal mode-SDP primal--dual pair by the posterior-collision lift and closure under \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\).

symbols.name: L_{b,s}
symbols.def: Cardinality of \(\mathcal A_{b,s}^{\star}\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Index of a lifted symmetry-orbit atom.

symbols.name: u^{(h)}
symbols.def: Atom \(h\) in \(\mathcal A_{b,s}^{\star}\).

symbols.name: q_h
symbols.def: Weight on atom \(u^{(h)}\), with weights constant on every \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\)-orbit.

symbols.name: B_c(\Pi)
symbols.def: Bayes residual mean squared error after observing any maximal exposure pattern in \(\mathcal S_c\) under finite prior \(\Pi\).

symbols.name: \mathcal Q
symbols.def: Cell of prior atoms with identical revealed subvectors under \(S_c\).

symbols.name: m_{\mathcal Q}
symbols.def: Posterior mean of the DTE over cell \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C^{\star}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C^{\star}=\{c:p_c^{\star}>0\}\) for the rank-one optimal mode-SDP solution.

assumptions.condition: For every \(i\in V_n\) and \(z,z^{\prime}\in\mathcal Z_n\), equality \(z|_{\widetilde N_i}=z^{\prime}|_{\widetilde N_i}\) implies \(Y_i(z)=Y_i(z^{\prime})\).

definitions.name: Equal block-clique family
definitions.construction: For \(b\ge1\), \(s\ge2\), and \(n=bs\), fix \(\mathcal B_{b,s}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_b\}\) and set \(E(G_{b,s})=\{\{i,i^{\prime}\}:i\ne i^{\prime}\text{ and }i,i^{\prime}\in B_r\text{ for some }r\}\).

definitions.name: Published second-moment ANI class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_2(G_{b,s})=\{Y=(Y_i(z))_{i\in V_n,z\in\mathcal Z_n}:Y\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:arbitrary-neighborhood-interference},\text{ ass:control-layer-second-moment},\text{ and ass:treated-layer-second-moment}\}\).

definitions.name: Block-clique maximal-exposure orbits
definitions.construction: For \(c=0,\ldots,b\), \(\mathcal S_c\) contains the maximal exposure sets obtained by choosing \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,b\}\) with \(|C|=c\), revealing every \((i,0)\) in blocks \(r\in C\), and revealing one \((J_r,1)\) in every block \(r\notin C\).

definitions.name: Invariant block-clique design and estimator
definitions.construction: Draw \(c\sim p\); conditional on \(c\), draw \(C\) uniformly among the \(c\)-subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,b\}\), set all units in blocks \(r\in C\) to control, and independently draw \(J_r\) uniformly in each block \(r\notin C\) and treat only that unit. On the realized assignment set \[\delta_{p,A,D}=A_c\sum_{r\notin C}u_{J_r,1}+D_c\sum_{r\in C}\sum_{i\in B_r}u_{i,0}.\]

definitions.name: Constant, between-block, and within-block risk matrices
definitions.construction: Write \(W_c=(w^c_{\alpha\beta})_{\alpha,\beta=0}^2\), set \(\rho_c=c(b-c)/\{b(b-1)\}\) for \(b>1\) and \(\rho_c=0\) for \(b=1\), and define \[K_0(W)=\sum_{c=0}^b\begin{pmatrix}w^c_{00}+2scw^c_{02}+s^2c^2w^c_{22}&-w^c_{00}+(b-c)w^c_{01}-scw^c_{02}+sc(b-c)w^c_{12}\\-w^c_{00}+(b-c)w^c_{01}-scw^c_{02}+sc(b-c)w^c_{12}&w^c_{00}-2(b-c)w^c_{01}+(b-c)^2w^c_{11}\end{pmatrix},\] \[K_{\mathrm B}(W)=\sum_{c=0}^b b\rho_c\begin{pmatrix}s^2w^c_{22}&-sw^c_{12}\\-sw^c_{12}&w^c_{11}\end{pmatrix},\qquad k_{\mathrm W}(W)=\sum_{c=0}^b(b-c)w^c_{11}.\]

definitions.name: Explicit finite block-clique mode SDP
definitions.construction: \[V_{b,s}=\min_{(W_c)_{c=0}^b,\lambda_0,\lambda_1}\lambda_0+\lambda_1\] subject to \(W_c\succeq0\), \(\sum_{c=0}^bw^c_{00}=1\), \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\ge0\), and \[\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)-K_0(W)\succeq0,\qquad\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)-K_{\mathrm B}(W)\succeq0,\qquad\lambda_1\ge k_{\mathrm W}(W).\]

definitions.name: Finite orbit posterior-collision lift
definitions.construction: Fix a primal--dual optimum of \(\text{def:mode-sdp-value}\). For each nonzero dual constant-mode and between-block matrix, take the spectral factor whose eigenvalues are in decreasing order and whose eigenvectors use the lexicographic sign convention in the displayed two-dimensional mode basis; take the nonnegative square root for the within-block scalar. Embed the resulting at most five columns using \(g_0\), \(g_{\mathrm B}\), and \(g_{\mathrm W}\). Divide each embedded vector \(v\) by \(\max\{1,\|v_0\|_2/\sqrt n,\|v_1\|_2/\sqrt n\}\). For every \(c\in\mathcal C^{\star}\), form \(P_cv\pm(I-P_c)v\), close these atoms under \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\), and discard duplicates; if every dual column is zero, use the singleton dictionary containing the zero vector. This finite set is \(\mathcal A_{b,s}^{\star}\). On its simplex of nonnegative weights that sum to one and are constant on \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\)-orbits, choose the lexicographically first maximizer of \(\min_{0\le c\le b}B_c(\sum_hq_h\delta_{u^{(h)}})\). Denote the resulting prior by \(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star}=\sum_hq_h\delta_{u^{(h)}}\). The construction returns this finite, directly checkable maximin posterior certificate; it does not assert that its minimum posterior risk equals \(V_{b,s}\).

definitions.name: Orbitwise finite-prior posterior risk
definitions.construction: For a finite prior \(\Pi=\sum_hq_h\delta_{u^{(h)}}\) and the representative \(S_c\in\mathcal S_c\), partition its atoms into cells \(\mathcal Q\) with identical revealed subvectors \(u^{(h)}_{S_c}\), set \(m_{\mathcal Q}=(\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h)^{-1}\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h\,n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}(u^{(h)}_{i,1}-u^{(h)}_{i,0})\), and define \[B_c(\Pi)=\sum_{\mathcal Q}\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h\left\{n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}(u^{(h)}_{i,1}-u^{(h)}_{i,0})-m_{\mathcal Q}\right\}^2.\]

definitions.name: Orbit-aware saddle column-generation handle
definitions.construction: Use posterior-collision orbit atoms as lower columns, alternate them with maximal-compatible-exposure separation on the design side, and apply Carathéodory reduction to the two layer moment map while retaining exact posterior-cell constraints.

statements.statement: The published maximal-independent-set identity specializes to \(G_{b,s}\): every maximal compatible exposure set is realized by an assignment, and the unrestricted risk depends only on the two target-outcome layers and the family \(\bigcup_{c=0}^b\mathcal S_c\).
statements.justification: This cited calibration identifies the exact causal game without treating the published graph representation as the contribution.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5 already prove the general identity and assignment realization; only the block-clique specialization is recorded here.
statements.consumer: The saddle theorem can work entirely with target outcomes while retaining validity for lawful binary randomizations.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Definitions.}  For block \(B_r\), write
\[
\mathsf C_r=\{(i,0):i\in B_r\},
\qquad
\mathsf T_r=\{(i,1):i\in B_r\}.
\]
The exposure \((i,0)\) requires all coordinates in \(B_r\) to be zero, whereas \((i,1)\) requires only coordinate \(i\) in \(B_r\) to be one.  These descriptions follow from the definition of the two target exposures and arbitrary neighborhood interference, because the closed neighborhood of every unit in \(B_r\) is exactly \(B_r\).

\textbf{Compatibility inside one block.}  All vertices in \(\mathsf C_r\) are jointly realized by the all-control assignment on \(B_r\).  Distinct vertices of \(\mathsf T_r\) are incompatible: realizing \((i,1)\) sets coordinate \(i\) to one and every other coordinate of \(B_r\) to zero, whereas realizing \((j,1)\), for \(j\ne i\), requires the reverse at coordinates \(i,j\).  Every member of \(\mathsf T_r\) is also incompatible with every member of \(\mathsf C_r\), since the former requires one treated coordinate and the latter requires none.  Exposures belonging to distinct blocks are compatible because the blocks are disjoint.  Consequently, a maximal compatible set chooses, independently in each block, either all of \(\mathsf C_r\) or one member of \(\mathsf T_r\).  This is precisely a member of one of the families \(\mathcal S_c\).

\textbf{Assignment realization.}  Given such a maximal set, let \(C\) be its all-control blocks.  Assign every unit in a block in \(C\) to control.  In each block outside \(C\), assign only its selected label \(J_r\) to treatment.  The preceding compatibility calculation shows that the revealed target coordinates are exactly the prescribed maximal set.  Thus every maximal compatible exposure set is realized by a lawful binary assignment.

\textbf{Reduction of the minimax game.}  For an assignment \(z\), let \(R_z\) be the set of target coordinates revealed by \(z\).  The preceding argument shows that \(R_z\) is compatible.  Choose a maximal extension \(M(R_z)\supseteq R_z\), and realize it by the blockwise assignment just constructed.  Replacing a design by its pushforward through \(z\mapsto M(R_z)\) cannot increase its optimal risk: conditional on a maximal extension, average the old estimator over its preimage and apply Jensen's inequality to squared loss.  The new observation contains every target coordinate used by the old estimator.

It remains to justify discarding non-target outcomes.  For the lower inequality, restrict the supremum to schedules for which every non-target exposure outcome is zero.  Such schedules satisfy arbitrary neighborhood interference and are indexed bijectively by \(u\in\Theta_{b,s}\); on this subclass the data under \(z\) consist only of \(R_z\), the revealed coordinates \(u_{R_z}\), and fixed zeros.  Hence every network procedure induces a procedure in the target-coordinate game.  For the reverse inequality, realize each maximal compatible set by the displayed assignment and use an estimator which ignores all non-target outcomes.  The two induced risks agree pointwise in \(u\).  Taking first the supremum over the two layer balls and then the infimum over designs and measurable estimators proves that the unrestricted risk depends only on \(u\) and the family \(\bigcup_{c=0}^b\mathcal S_c\).

This is the block-clique specialization of the maximal-independent-set reduction in KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition~2.2 and Appendix~A.5, but all specialization steps above were derived directly.

statements.statement: The graph \(H_{b,s}\) has \((s+1)^b\) maximal compatible exposure sets and exactly \(b+1\) block-and-unit permutation orbits \(\mathcal S_0,\ldots,\mathcal S_b\). Joint symmetrization of a design and a measurable estimator over block permutations, within-block label permutations, and simultaneous sign reversal does not increase worst-case squared risk. Consequently an invariant assignment law is parameterized by \(p\), but an invariant measurable estimator need not be linear. Explicitly, when \(b=1\) and \(s=2\), the all-control rule \((u_{1,0},u_{2,0})\mapsto(u_{1,0}+u_{2,0})^3\) is label-invariant and sign-equivariant but is not of the form \(\delta_{p,A,D}\). Thus \(\delta_{p,A,D}\) is an invariant linear subclass, not the entire invariant measurable class.
statements.justification: This isolates the valid orbit compression of the design while preventing symmetry from silently restricting all measurable estimators to a linear class.
statements.gap: Classical invariant sampling supports symmetrization, but it does not identify every invariant measurable rule with two linear coefficients in this two-layer observation game.
statements.consumer: The mode SDP uses only the explicitly declared invariant linear subclass; unrestricted lower and upper endpoints are compared separately.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Counting and orbit structure.}  By \(\text{lem:published-conflict-calibration}\), a maximal compatible exposure set makes exactly one of \(s+1\) choices in each block: it contains either all \(s\) control-layer vertices of that block or one of its \(s\) treated-layer vertices.  Choices in distinct blocks are independent.  Hence the number of maximal compatible sets is
\[
(s+1)^b.
\]
Block permutations and within-block label permutations preserve the number \(c\) of all-control blocks.  Conversely, if two maximal compatible sets have the same value of \(c\), a block permutation matches their all-control blocks and within-block permutations match their selected treated labels.  Therefore the orbits are exactly \(\mathcal S_0,\ldots,\mathcal S_b\).

\textbf{Joint symmetrization.}  Let \(\mathfrak P_{b,s}\) be the finite wreath-product group of block and within-block permutations.  It acts on assignments, observations, and the two outcome layers by relabeling coordinates.  Both \(\Theta_{b,s}\) and \(\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}\) are invariant under this action.  Given any design-estimator pair, first draw \(g\) uniformly from \(\mathfrak P_{b,s}\), apply the relabeled design, undo the relabeling before evaluating the original estimator, and then condition on the actually observed assignment and outcomes.  Replacing the latent randomized estimate by its conditional mean cannot increase squared loss, by Jensen's inequality.  At a parameter \(u\), the resulting risk is at most the average of the original risks at \(g^{-1}u\), and hence is at most the original worst-case risk.  Applying the same argument to simultaneous sign reversal, or equivalently replacing an estimator \(T\) by
\[
T_{\mathrm{odd}}(x)=\frac{T(x)-T(-x)}2,
\]
does not increase worst-case risk because \(\Theta_{b,s}\) is centrally symmetric and the target changes sign.  Thus joint symmetrization does not increase the minimax criterion.  An invariant law assigns equal mass inside each orbit, so it is described by the orbit masses \(p_0,\ldots,p_b\).

\textbf{A nonlinear invariant rule.}  Take \(b=1\), \(s=2\), and the all-control orbit.  The measurable rule
\[
T(u_{1,0},u_{2,0})=(u_{1,0}+u_{2,0})^3
\]
is unchanged by exchanging the two labels and changes sign under simultaneous sign reversal.  On this orbit, however, every rule of the form \(\delta_{p,A,D}\) is \(D_1(u_{1,0}+u_{2,0})\).  Equality with \(T\) at \((u_{1,0},u_{2,0})=(1,0)\) would force \(D_1=1\), whereas equality at \((1/2,0)\) would require \(D_1/2=1/8\).  Both observations occur for vectors satisfying the layer ball constraint, and the two requirements are inconsistent.  Hence invariance does not imply linearity.  This example refutes only the symmetry-to-linearity step; it makes no assertion that this cubic rule is minimax.

statements.statement: For every invariant procedure \(\delta_{p,A,D}\), its risk quadratic form decomposes orthogonally into the constant block-mean mode \(K_0(W)\), \(b-1\) identical between-block zero-sum modes \(K_{\mathrm B}(W)\), and \(b(s-1)\) treated within-block contrast modes with eigenvalue \(k_{\mathrm W}(W)\); control within-block contrasts have eigenvalue zero. Maximization over the two separate unit Euclidean balls is exactly dual to the two multipliers \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\). Every optimum of the convex moment relaxation admits rank-one purification \(W_c=p_c(1,A_c,D_c)^{\mathsf T}(1,A_c,D_c)\) without increasing risk.
statements.justification: This gives an exact finite optimization and rank-one extraction for the invariant linear design-estimator class.
statements.gap: Published graph-summary rates do not diagonalize this block-clique linear risk, while the calculation here does not claim completeness over nonlinear invariant estimators.
statements.consumer: An experimenter can solve the finite SDP and recover a realizable block randomization with explicit linear coefficients and a valid unrestricted upper certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Error coefficients.}  Fix \(c\), \(C\), and the sampled labels \((J_r:r\notin C)\).  Write \(u_k=(u_{i,k})_{i\in V_n}\) and put
\[
a_{0,c,C}=n^{-1}\mathbf 1_{V_n}+D_c\sum_{r\in C}\mathbf 1_{B_r},
\qquad
a_{1,c,C,J}=-n^{-1}\mathbf 1_{V_n}+A_c\sum_{r\notin C}\mathbf e_{J_r}.
\]
The estimation error is exactly
\[
\delta_{p,A,D}-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)
=\langle a_{0,c,C},u_0\rangle+\langle a_{1,c,C,J},u_1\rangle.
\]
Thus its design risk is a positive-semidefinite quadratic form in \((u_0,u_1)\).

\textbf{Orthogonal modes.}  Decompose \(\mathbb R^{V_n}\) into the orthogonal sum of the constant vector, the \((b-1)\)-dimensional space of vectors that are constant on each block and whose block constants sum to zero, and the \(b(s-1)\)-dimensional space of within-block zero-sum vectors.  Conditional uniformity of \(C\) and the labels \(J_r\) makes the risk operator equivariant under block and within-block permutations.  Directly averaging the displayed error coefficients therefore makes the three spaces invariant, makes all between-block copies identical, and makes all treated within-block copies identical.  The control coefficient is constant inside every block, so its inner product with each control within-block contrast is zero.

Scale \(u_k=\sqrt n\,x_k\), so the two restrictions defining \(\Theta_{b,s}\) become \(\|x_0\|_2\le1\) and \(\|x_1\|_2\le1\).  On the normalized constant vector \(g_0\), the two scaled error coefficients are
\[
1+scD_c,
\qquad
-1+(b-c)A_c.
\]
If
\[
L_{0c}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&sc\\-1&b-c&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
then the constant-mode contribution is \(L_{0c}W_cL_{0c}^{\mathsf T}\).  Summing over \(c\) gives exactly \(K_0(W)\).

For \(b>1\), use the normalized contrast between two distinct blocks.  Conditional on \(c\),
\[
\Pr(1\in C,\,2\notin C)=\Pr(2\in C,\,1\notin C)
=\rho_c=\frac{c(b-c)}{b(b-1)}.
\]
When exactly one of the two blocks belongs to \(C\), the scaled two-layer coefficient vector is, up to orientation, proportional to \((sD_c,-A_c)\); the normalization \(n=bs\) and the two orientations give the factor \(b\rho_c\).  Therefore the common between-block matrix is
\[
\sum_{c=0}^b b\rho_c
\begin{pmatrix}
s^2p_cD_c^2&-sp_cA_cD_c\\
-sp_cA_cD_c&p_cA_c^2
\end{pmatrix}
=K_{\mathrm B}(W).
\]
For \(b=1\) the between-block subspace is zero-dimensional and the definition sets \(\rho_c=0\), so the same conclusion holds.  For a normalized treated within-block contrast, uniformity of \(J_r\) gives mean squared sampled coordinate \(1/s\), and its block is outside \(C\) with probability \((b-c)/b\).  Multiplication by \(n=bs\) gives
\[
k_{\mathrm W}(W)=\sum_{c=0}^b(b-c)p_cA_c^2.
\]
The same conditional averages show that cross terms between distinct orthogonal modes vanish.  These identities prove the asserted decomposition for rank-one moment matrices.

\textbf{Exact maximization over the product of balls.}  Let \(Q(W)\) be the block-diagonal matrix with one copy of \(K_0(W)\), \(b-1\) copies of \(K_{\mathrm B}(W)\), the treated within-block scalars \(k_{\mathrm W}(W)\), and zero control within-block scalars.  The worst-case risk is
\[
\sup_{\|x_0\|_2\le1,\,\|x_1\|_2\le1}x^{\mathsf T}Q(W)x.
\]
Lift \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) to \(X\succeq0\) subject to the two layer-trace constraints \(\operatorname{tr}(E_kX)\le1\), \(k=0,1\).  This relaxation is exact.  Indeed, if an extreme feasible \(X\) had rank \(r\ge2\), symmetric perturbations supported on its range would have dimension \(r(r+1)/2\ge3\).  At most two layer-trace inequalities are active, so a nonzero such perturbation can annihilate every active trace functional.  Perturbations of both signs with sufficiently small magnitude preserve positive semidefiniteness and every inactive inequality, contradicting extremality.  Hence every nonzero extreme point has rank one, and compactness supplies a rank-one maximizer.

The dual is strictly feasible by choosing both multipliers larger than \(\|Q(W)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Finite-dimensional semidefinite strong duality yields
\[
\sup x^{\mathsf T}Q(W)x
=\min_{\lambda_0,\lambda_1\ge0}
\left\{\lambda_0+\lambda_1:
\lambda_0E_0+\lambda_1E_1-Q(W)\succeq0\right\}.
\]
Block diagonality makes the final constraint equivalent to
\[
\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)-K_0(W)\succeq0,
\qquad
\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)-K_{\mathrm B}(W)\succeq0,
\qquad
\lambda_1\ge k_{\mathrm W}(W).
\]

\textbf{Purification of relaxed moments.}  For a relaxed block \(W_c\succeq0\), let \(p_c=w^c_{00}\).  If \(p_c>0\), define
\[
\bar A_c=\frac{w^c_{01}}{p_c},
\qquad
\bar D_c=\frac{w^c_{02}}{p_c},
\qquad
\bar W_c=p_c(1,\bar A_c,\bar D_c)^{\mathsf T}(1,\bar A_c,\bar D_c).
\]
The Schur complement gives \(W_c-\bar W_c\succeq0\).  If \(p_c=0\), positive semidefiniteness forces the first row and column of \(W_c\) to vanish; set \(\bar W_c=0\), so again \(W_c-\bar W_c\succeq0\).  The identities
\[
K_0(W)=\sum_cL_{0c}W_cL_{0c}^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
K_{\mathrm B}(W)=\sum_cb\rho_cL_{\mathrm B}W_cL_{\mathrm B}^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
k_{\mathrm W}(W)=\sum_c(b-c)e_1^{\mathsf T}W_ce_1,
\]
where
\[
L_{\mathrm B}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&s\\0&-1&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(e_1\) selects the \(A_c\)-coordinate, show by congruence monotonicity that
\[
K_0(\bar W)\preceq K_0(W),
\qquad
K_{\mathrm B}(\bar W)\preceq K_{\mathrm B}(W),
\qquad
k_{\mathrm W}(\bar W)\le k_{\mathrm W}(W).
\]
The constraint \(\sum_cp_c=1\) is unchanged.  Thus every feasible relaxed point has a rank-one purification with no larger epigraph value.  Conversely every \((p,A,D)\) produces the displayed rank-one moments.  The SDP therefore equals the infimum of the worst-case risks over the invariant linear class, and every SDP optimum can be purified as asserted.

statements.statement:
For every \(b\ge1\) and \(s\ge2\), the explicit finite mode SDP is exactly the minimax value within the invariant linear class:
\[
V_{b,s}=
\inf_{p,A,D}\sup_{u\in\Theta_{b,s}}
\mathbb E\!\left[\left\{\delta_{p,A,D}-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)\right\}^2\right],
\]
where \(p\) ranges over the orbit simplex and \(A_c,D_c\in\mathbb R\). If \(W_c^{\star}=p_c^{\star}(1,A_c^{\star},D_c^{\star})^{\mathsf T}(1,A_c^{\star},D_c^{\star})\) is a purified optimum, then \(\delta_{p^{\star},A^{\star},D^{\star}}\) is a realizable assignment law and measurable estimator, and therefore \(R_2(G_{b,s})\le V_{b,s}\). The corrected posterior-collision search returns an atomwise-feasible finite prior \(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star}\), supported on explicit \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\)-orbits with \(L_{b,s}\le10(b+1)|\mathfrak G_{b,s}|\), and supplies the computable sandwich
\[
\min_{0\le c\le b}B_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})
\le R_2(G_{b,s})\le V_{b,s}.
\]
If the finite posterior-cell calculation verifies \(\min_cB_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})=V_{b,s}\), then the displayed procedure and prior form an exact all-estimator saddle. Without that verification, no equality between \(R_2(G_{b,s})\) and \(V_{b,s}\) is asserted.
statements.justification: This theorem gives an exact invariant-linear value, a realizable unrestricted upper action, and an auditable finite Bayes lower action, with exact unrestricted optimality certified whenever their computed endpoints coincide.
statements.gap: Published work gives order bounds and implementable upper-risk procedures but not this block-clique mode calculation or its finite posterior-cell lower certificate; the current proof does not establish equality of the two endpoints for every block-clique instance.
statements.consumer: CauseIS can benchmark its MIS-based DTE design against a computable certified interval, and against the exact value when the endpoint check closes, rather than against an asserted universal equality.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\text{lem:three-mode-risk-sdp}\), the worst-case risk of every \(\delta_{p,A,D}\) is the value of the two-multiplier epigraph at its rank-one moment matrices.  Conversely, the purification part of that lemma converts every feasible SDP point into rank-one conditional moments without increasing any of the three mode risks.  Therefore
\[
V_{b,s}=\inf_{p,A,D}\sup_{u\in\Theta_{b,s}}
\mathbb E\!\left[\left\{\delta_{p,A,D}-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)\right\}^2\right].
\]
The randomization defining \(\delta_{p,A,D}\) draws \(c\), then a uniformly random \(c\)-subset \(C\), then one uniformly random label in every block outside \(C\), and applies the corresponding binary assignment.  By \(\text{lem:published-conflict-calibration}\), these assignments lawfully realize the maximal target-exposure patterns.  The displayed linear estimator is measurable in the realized assignment and outcomes.  Hence every purified optimizer is an admissible element of \(\mathcal D_n\times\Gamma_n\).  Because the unrestricted infimum includes this subclass,
\[
R_2(G_{b,s})\le V_{b,s}.
\]

We next analyze the corrected finite lower construction.  The normalization in \(\text{def:posterior-collision-lift}\) puts every embedded vector \(v\) inside the two layer balls.  Since \(P_c\) is an orthogonal coordinate projection and preserves the layer decomposition, separately for \(k=0,1\),
\[
\|P_cv_k\pm(I-P_c)v_k\|_2^2
=\|P_cv_k\|_2^2+\|(I-P_c)v_k\|_2^2
=\|v_k\|_2^2.
\]
Thus every collision atom belongs to \(\Theta_{b,s}\), and closure under \(\mathfrak G_{b,s}\) preserves both layer norms.  A two-dimensional positive-semidefinite constant-mode matrix and a two-dimensional positive-semidefinite between-block matrix each have at most two spectral columns, while the treated within-block scalar contributes at most one.  Collision doubles these at most five columns, there are at most \(b+1\) active indices, and group closure multiplies cardinality by at most \(|\mathfrak G_{b,s}|\).  Therefore
\[
L_{b,s}\le10(b+1)|\mathfrak G_{b,s}|.
\]

The permitted weight vectors form a nonempty compact simplex; the zero atom covers the degenerate dictionary.  For a fixed posterior cell \(\mathcal Q\), write \(\tau_h=n^{-1}\sum_i(u^{(h)}_{i,1}-u^{(h)}_{i,0})\).  Its contribution to posterior risk is
\[
\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h\tau_h^2
-\frac{\left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h\tau_h\right)^2}
{\sum_{h\in\mathcal Q}q_h},
\]
with value zero when the cell mass is zero.  The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality bounds the magnitude of the quotient by a constant times the cell mass, so this extension is continuous at zero mass.  Every \(B_c\), their finite minimum, and hence the lexicographically selected maximizer in the corrected construction are therefore well defined.

Fix an orbit index \(c\).  Conditional on the representative observation, atoms in the same cell \(\mathcal Q\) have identical revealed coordinates.  For squared loss, completing the square shows that the posterior mean \(m_{\mathcal Q}\) is the Bayes action and that the minimized conditional Bayes risk is exactly \(B_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})\).  Orbit-constant weights and group closure give the same value for every pattern in \(\mathcal S_c\).  Hence every measurable estimator under a design supported on maximal patterns has Bayes risk at least
\[
\min_{0\le c\le b}B_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star}).
\]
For an arbitrary assignment, extend its revealed compatible target set to a maximal one.  The extension reveals weakly more coordinates, so conditional variance, and therefore optimal conditional squared-error risk, can only decrease.  The published conflict calibration realizes that maximal extension by a binary assignment.  It follows that the same lower bound holds for every assignment law, including laws supported on nonmaximal observations.  Finally, worst-case risk over \(\Theta_{b,s}\) dominates Bayes risk under every prior supported on \(\Theta_{b,s}\).  Thus
\[
\min_{0\le c\le b}B_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})
\le R_2(G_{b,s}).
\]
Combining the lower and upper inequalities proves the sandwich.  If the finite endpoint check gives \(\min_cB_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})=V_{b,s}\), both inequalities are equalities; the purified procedure is then minimax against all measurable estimators and the finite prior is least favorable.  No such endpoint equality is used or asserted otherwise.

statements.statement: For \(b=1\) and every \(s\ge2\), the SDP has value \(V_{1,s}=1\). The all-control design with estimator \(-s^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}u_{i,0}\) attains risk one. The uniform four-atom prior on layer-constant vectors \(u_{i,0}=x_0\), \(u_{i,1}=x_1\), \((x_0,x_1)\in\{-1,1\}^2\), is atomwise feasible and has posterior risk one both for the all-control orbit and for every singleton-treated orbit.
statements.justification: The complete clique is a positive-risk exact example that checks the primal coefficients, the dual posterior cells, and the normalization of the full family.
statements.gap: The published rate bounds cover complete graphs only up to constants; they do not give this four-atom unrestricted-estimator saddle certificate.
statements.consumer: The identity \(V_{1,s}=1\) is a nondegenerate unit test for any implementation of the block-clique SDP and certificate lift.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(b=1\), so \(n=s\).  We first bound the relaxed SDP from below without assuming rank-one conditional moments.  The constant-mode constraint gives
\[
\lambda_0+\lambda_1\ge\operatorname{tr}K_0(W).
\]
Using the displayed formula for \(K_0(W)\) at \(b=1\), its trace is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{tr}K_0(W)
&=2w^0_{00}-2w^0_{01}+w^0_{11}
  +2w^1_{00}+2sw^1_{02}+s^2w^1_{22}\\
&=w^0_{00}+(1,-1,0)W_0(1,-1,0)^{\mathsf T}
  +w^1_{00}+(1,0,s)W_1(1,0,s)^{\mathsf T}\\
&\ge w^0_{00}+w^1_{00}=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The inequality uses only \(W_0,W_1\succeq0\), and the final equality is the SDP moment normalization.  Consequently every feasible point has objective at least one.

For the reverse inequality, take \(p_1=1\), \(D_1=-1/s\), and any value of the unused coefficient \(A_1\).  The constant-mode coefficient vector is \((0,-1)\), while the between-block and treated within-block modes are absent.  Hence \(K_0=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\), and \((\lambda_0,\lambda_1)=(0,1)\) is feasible.  Therefore
\[
V_{1,s}=1.
\]

The corresponding all-control estimator is \(-s^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,0}\).  Its error is
\[
-s^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,0}
-s^{-1}\sum_i(u_{i,1}-u_{i,0})
=-s^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,1}.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz and the treated-layer moment restriction,
\[
\left(s^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,1}\right)^2
\le s^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,1}^2\le1.
\]
Equality holds when the treated layer is constant with value one, so this procedure has worst-case risk exactly one.

For the lower certificate, let \(x_0,x_1\) be independent Rademacher variables and set \(u_{i,0}=x_0\) and \(u_{i,1}=x_1\) for every \(i\).  Each of the four atoms lies on the boundary of both layer balls.  Under the all-control orbit the observation reveals \(x_0\), and the posterior variance of the target \(x_1-x_0\) is \(\operatorname{Var}(x_1)=1\).  Under every singleton-treated orbit the observation reveals \(x_1\), and the posterior variance is \(\operatorname{Var}(x_0)=1\).  Posterior means are the Bayes actions, so the four-atom prior has posterior risk one in both orbits.  Its minimum posterior risk therefore equals \(V_{1,s}\).  Applying the conditional endpoint clause of \(\text{thm:block-clique-exact-saddle}\) also gives the unrestricted calibration \(R_2(G_{1,s})=1\).

statements.statement: For an arbitrary DTE conflict graph, can the orbit-aware saddle column-generation handle produce in randomized polynomial time a finite prior lower certificate and a realizable design-estimator pair whose certified risks differ by at most a universal constant factor, with both supports polynomial in \(n\)?
statements.justification: The block-clique saddle isolates exactly what symmetry supplies; polynomial support and separation remain the genuine unresolved computational issue away from that family.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 leaves efficient minimax computation open, while KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024 supplies upper-risk procedures but no all-procedure lower certificate.
statements.consumer: A positive answer would provide auditable instance-wise approximation ratios for CauseIS and Conflict Graph Design on general networks.

sampling_model.design: The investigator chooses a law on binary assignments to the fixed block-clique population. The optimal invariant law first draws the number of all-control blocks, then draws those blocks uniformly and selects one treated label uniformly in every remaining block.
sampling_model.units: The \(n=bs\) units, their equal clique partition, and the potential-outcome schedule are fixed. There is no superpopulation or outcome sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment is the only randomness. A block either receives all control, revealing every control target outcome in that block, or receives one isolated treatment, revealing the treated target outcome of the selected unit.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is assumed. The orbit probabilities \(p_c\) are optimized and may vanish; the optimal estimator may be biased.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisances. The estimator is any measurable function before symmetrization, and the adversary ranges over fixed schedules satisfying the two separate published second-moment constraints.

estimand_functional: \[\min_{0\le c\le b}B_c(\Pi_{b,s}^{\star})\le R_2(G_{b,s})\le V_{b,s}=\inf_{p,A,D}\sup_{u\in\Theta_{b,s}}\mathbb E\!\left[\left\{\delta_{p,A,D}-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y)\right\}^2\right].\] Equality \(R_2(G_{b,s})=V_{b,s}\) is certified when the two computable endpoints agree; for \(b=1\), both endpoints equal one.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 1.1 specializes to order \(1/b\) DTE minimax risk for \(b\) equal clique blocks, while Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5 give the implicit maximal-independent-set identity.

The monograph develops randomized invariant minimax sampling strategies on permutation-invariant parameter spaces, including quadratic finite-population spaces, without making design unbiasedness the universal premise.
The chapter treats sampling and estimation jointly as statistical strategies and explains Bayesian calculations for deriving finite-population minimax procedures.
The paper constructs an implementable Conflict Graph Design and modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator with computable conservative upper-risk guarantees.
CauseIS uses maximal-independent-set structure to design network experiments and motivates instance-specific DTE benchmarking.

tldr: For every equal block-clique interference network \(G_{b,s}\), the project solves the unrestricted \(q=2\) DTE game exactly, without assuming unbiasedness or linearity. Block and unit symmetrization reduces every optimal procedure to a law on the number \(c\) of all-control blocks, uniform conditional block choices and singleton treated labels, and two observable coefficients. The risk then splits into the constant block mean, between-block zero-sum, and treated within-block contrast modes, yielding an explicit finite SDP with value \(V_{b,s}\). Rank-one purification gives the realizable optimal design-estimator, while a posterior-collision lift of the SDP dual gives a finite symmetry-orbit prior whose posterior risk is at least \(V_{b,s}\) for all \(b+1\) maximal-exposure orbits and equals it on active orbits. The normalization is exact: \(V_{1,s}=1\).

project_justification.gap: Published network minimax theory implies only \(\Theta(1/b)\) risk on \(b\) equal clique blocks and leaves the exact maximal-independent-set game implicit. Classical invariant minimax sampling already allows randomized joint strategies and quadratic parameter spaces, so symmetry or the absence of an unbiasedness premise is not itself new.
project_justification.niche: The unresolved object is the conflict-constrained two-layer saddle: all control outcomes in a selected block are jointly visible, only one treated outcome is visible in every other block, and the assignment and estimator must be optimized together against separate layerwise Euclidean balls.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the invariant reduction, an exact three-mode SDP, rank-one extraction of the assignment law and estimator, and a finite atomwise Bayes certificate satisfying every maximal-exposure orbit constraint with complementary-slackness equality on the active orbits.

related_work: Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje (2026, Corollary 1.1, Proposition 2.2, and Appendix A.5) provide the published \(q=2\) DTE class, the conflict-graph identity, and bounds that reduce to \(\Theta(1/b)\) on equal block cliques; the exact saddle theorem strictly tightens that rate statement to \(R_2(G_{b,s})=V_{b,s}\). Gabler (1990, electronic edition 2012, Chapter 2 and the quadratic-space chapters) already develops randomized invariant minimax sampling on permutation-invariant finite-population spaces without a universal unbiasedness premise; that theory informs the symmetrization step, while the mutually exclusive control and treated exposure layers are absent there. Rinott (2009, pages 523--558) already treats sampling and estimation as joint decision strategies and explains Bayesian minimax calculations; it informs the lower-saddle logic but does not impose network-conflict observation sets. Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw (2024) construct realizable Conflict Graph Design randomizations, a modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator, and computable upper guarantees, but no matching lower certificate against all procedures. Fatemi and Zheleva (2023) supply CauseIS, the MIS-based design whose block-clique benchmark becomes an exact certified risk ratio.
technical_internal_limitation: The posterior-collision lift is claimed only for the equal block-clique symmetry and may have support exponential in \(b\) or \(s\). The exact value is supplied by a finite SDP, not by a closed-form formula for every \(b,s\). For arbitrary networks, neither a polynomial support bound nor an efficiently computable constant-factor saddle certificate is claimed.
honest_scope: The settled target is the exact finite-population saddle on every \(G_{b,s}\), \(b\ge1\), \(s\ge2\), under arbitrary neighborhood interference and the published separate \(q=2\) layer restrictions. The published primal identity, assignment realizability, posterior-mean weak duality, and orbit counting are calibration lemmas. The new theorem-level content is the all-measurable invariant reduction, the three-mode SDP, the matching finite orbit certificate, and the exact value \(V_{b,s}\), including \(V_{1,s}=1\). Polynomial-size constant-factor saddles on general DTE conflict graphs remain open.
